# The World Remembers

An interactive, sourced storybook that retells ancient accounts in their own voices and places relevant written, archaeological, and scientific records alongside them. The book has 17 chapters, 202 source cards, 41 artifact records, 134 evidence-lens cards, and 12 manuscript-witness profiles across 37 catalogued cultures.

## Reading order

1. Creation — Out of the Deep
2. The Garden
3. From Two to a World — The Plateau
4. The Watchers
5. The Giants
6. The Great Flood
7. The Kinds — What the Vessel Was For
8. The Ark — A Vessel by Measure
9. The Tower
10. The Reset
11. The Second Flood — The Long War Against the Giants
12. The House of David — One Family, One City
13. The Dragon — The Deep Subdued
14. The God Who Returns
15. Mazzaroth — The Ordered Sky
16. The World Remembers
17. The Witnesses

## World atlas

The atlas compares dates from Sebastian C. Adams's 1881 synchronological chart with independently dated regional periods, sites, and the Mawmluh Cave climate proxy. The chart places the “Confusion of Tongues” and dispersion at 2247 BC. The formal 4.2 ka boundary is approximately 2250 BCE, a modeled midpoint within a local isotope excursion extending over centuries. The atlas shows these date labels together while keeping their different dating methods visible. Its main story horizon ends at 70 CE; later manuscripts are source provenance dates.

## Reading and citation policy

Biblical quotations use NASB 1995. Other textual witnesses and translation variants are identified separately; they are not silently substituted into a NASB quotation.

Each source card carries the era the tradition speaks of and the date of the surviving text that carries it. Quotation and paraphrase labels are explicit. The accounts are given as their authors gave them, not re-labelled as myth; a late or post-contact record is dated on its card rather than discounted. The atlas's regional bands show what was happening in each region at the same time, each row with its own dating method.
